newsitem.title: USA: Balanced budget amendment a terrible mistake - Rubin.
newsitem.headline: Balanced budget amendment a terrible mistake - Rubin.

text.p: Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin on Sunday reiterated his opposition to a balanced budget amendment to the constitution, saying it would be a "terrible mistake."
Interviewed on ABC television's "This Week" news program, Rubin argued that the amendment would pose risks for both the economy and the state-run Social Security pension program.

If a balanced budget amendment has to be passed, it should exclude the Social Security surplus and not count that as part of the budget, he said. That would mean the budget would have to be cut even more if it were to be balanced.

If the proposed amedment clears Congress by the two-thirds vote in each house, it will have seven years to win ratification by 38 of the 50 states. Although President Clinton opposes it, he cannot veto a constitutional amendment.
Echoing comments made earlier by White House budget director Franklin Raines, Rubin said that Clinton plans to propose some $100 billion in tax cuts in his upcoming budget.
Rubin said the tax cuts will be permanent if the economy performs as the administration expects over the coming five years.
